column1: # Spec 59 known differences: a case XLibur is known to answer differently from Excel. function, case id, xlibur answer, excel answer, reason, issue.
# A row must carry a reason. The runner fails on a row that now agrees, and on one whose XLibur answer changed.

column5: AND("") is #VALUE! in Excel and TRUE in XLibur
Excel returns the real cube root for a negative base with exponent 1/3; XLibur returns #NUM!
Excel rounds 1.005 to 1.01; XLibur rounds the binary value to 1 (Excel probably rounds the 15-digit decimal form)
Excel returns exactly 0 for SUM(0.1,0.2)-0.3; XLibur returns the IEEE residue
=GCD(A1) with an empty cell reference: Excel returns error:#VALUE!; XLibur returns number:0
=LCM(A1) with an empty cell reference: Excel returns error:#VALUE!; XLibur returns number:0
=LCM(4,A1) with an empty cell reference: Excel returns number:4; XLibur returns number:0
=OR("5") with a direct text argument: Excel returns #VALUE!; XLibur returns FALSE
=OR("x") with a direct text argument: Excel returns #VALUE!; XLibur returns FALSE
=OR("") with a direct text argument: Excel returns #VALUE!; XLibur returns FALSE
=OR("0") with a direct text argument: Excel returns #VALUE!; XLibur returns FALSE
ROMAN(1999,TRUE) is MCMXCIX in Excel and MLMVLIV in XLibur: the boolean form argument is read differently
SUMPRODUCT of a range and an error: Excel returns #N/A; XLibur returns #VALUE!
TYPE of a multi-cell range in a single cell: Excel returns 1 (the intersected cell); XLibur returns 64 (array)
Excel returns error:#N/A; XLibur returns error:#REF!
Excel returns error:#N/A; XLibur returns error:#REF!
Excel refuses =RANK(3,{1,2,3}) at entry; XLibur accepts it and returns number:1

RATE(10,0,800) is 800(1+r)^10=0, whose only root is r=-1 (ten-fold), so XLibur gives #NUM! like any rate at or below -1. Excel stops short of -1 where its step rule fires, and the answer moves with the guess: -0.999998742518659 by default, -0.9999987245009726 from -0.5, -0.9999987194570075 from 0.5 (Excel 16.0)
